page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-32GB is a Cloud Native virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 4 vCPUs, which correspond to 4 physical cores operating at 2.0 GHz with a shared CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. No local storage or dedicated GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile. The shared AMD EPYC processor delivers poor single-core CPU performance of 785.98 and weak multi-core performance of 3132.76 in stress-ng tests. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is average at 411.23 GB/sec, but drops to a weak 27.8 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. PassMark testing places the CPU score at 8150.98, memory score at 2271.64, and database operations at 2795.16, all falling into the average tier. However, real-world application throughput is limited, as shown by a poor static web serving throughput of 2.52 GB/sec and weak Redis SET performance at 5.78 million operations per second.

This server offers a high memory capacity relative to its vCPU count, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring substantial RAM without demanding intense, dedicated CPU compute cycles. The shared CPU allocation presents a tradeoff, resulting in lower computational performance and poor throughput for intensive tasks like medium-scale LLM inference, where the 7B model prompt processing reaches only 14.74 tokens/sec. Consequently, this configuration is best suited for memory-heavy but compute-light workloads, such as caching layers, lightweight database operations, and basic memory-intensive data processing.
